<hr style="box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<h3 id="background" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">BACKGROUND</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Many of the Projects in CS6035 are focused on offensive security tasks. These are related to <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_team">Red Team</a> activities/tasks that many of us may associate with cybersecurity. This project will be focused on defensive security tasks, which are usually considered <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_team_(computer_security)">Blue Team</a> activities that are done by many corporate teams.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Historically, many defensive security professionals have investigated malicious activity, files, and code. They investigate these to create patterns (often called signatures) that can be used to detect (and prevent) malicious activity, files, and code when that pattern is used again. What this means is that these simple methods only were effective on known threats.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">This approach was relatively effective in preventing known malware from infecting systems, but it did nothing to protect against novel attacks. As attackers became more sophisticated, they learned to tweak or simply encode their malicious activity, files, or code to avoid detection from these simple pattern matching detections.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">With this background information, it would be nice if a more general solution could give a score to activity, files, and code that pass through corporate systems every day. This solution would inform the security team that while a certain pattern may not exactly fit a signature of known malicious activity, files, or code it appears to be very similar to examples that were seen in the past that were malicious.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Luckily machine learning models can do exactly that if provided with proper training data! Thus, it is no surprise that one of the most powerful tools in the hands of defensive cybersecurity professionals is Machine Learning. Modern detection systems usually use a combination of machine learning models and pattern matching (regular expressions) to detect and prevent malicious activity on networks and devices.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">This project will focus on teaching the fundamentals of data analysis and building/testing your own machine learning models in python. You’ll be using the open source libraries Pandas and Scikit-Learn.

<hr style="box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<h2 id="why-traditional-machine-learning-still-matters-in-cybersecurity" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">Why Traditional Machine Learning Still Matters in Cybersecurity</h2>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Large language models (LLMs) and other generative AI systems are larger, more capable, and more generally intelligent than the traditional machine learning models used in many security products. However, more intelligence is not always the most important requirement for a security decision. Traditional models such as logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines are still widely used because they can be designed for a specific task and operated efficiently at very large scale.

<h3 id="speed-and-inference-cost" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Speed and Inference Cost</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Cybersecurity systems often analyze enormous streams of data: network connections, authentication events, email messages, endpoint activity, and file metadata. A small classifier can make a prediction in milliseconds using limited CPU or memory. This makes it practical to score every event close to where it occurs, including on an endpoint or in a high-volume cloud service.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">An LLM generally requires substantially more memory and compute for each inference. Sending every event to a large hosted model can also introduce network delay, service limits, and per-request charges. Even when an LLM is technically able to classify an event, a traditional model may be fast enough to inspect all events rather than only a sample. That difference matters when a missed event could be the first sign of an attack.

<h3 id="training-and-fine-tuning-costs" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Training and Fine-Tuning Costs</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Traditional models are often inexpensive to train and can be retrained regularly as an organization’s data changes. A security team may be able to train a model on local hardware using a labeled dataset, then update it as new malware families or normal user behaviors appear. The data pipeline, model size, and training process can also be easier to reproduce.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Training or fine-tuning an LLM usually requires specialized hardware, more data preparation, and substantially more time and money. Using a hosted model can reduce the infrastructure burden, but it may add recurring costs and create questions about how sensitive security data is handled. For a narrowly defined prediction, the additional training investment may not produce a benefit proportional to its cost.

<h3 id="predictability-and-interpretability" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Predictability and Interpretability</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Security systems frequently need stable, testable behavior. A traditional classifier can return a probability or score from a known set of facts and the team can choose a threshold that determines whether an event is allowed, blocked, or sent to an analyst. The same input and model version should produce the same result, which makes regression testing and incident investigations easier.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Generative models produce text and can sometimes be inconsistent or confidently wrong. Their outputs can depend on prompts, context, model versions, and sampling settings. It can be difficult to prove why an LLM reached a particular conclusion, and an LLM may generate a plausible explanation that does not accurately describe its internal reasoning.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">One recent example shows how attackers can deliberately exploit LLM based defenses. Researchers reported that Russia-aligned UAC-0099 malware included strings referring to nuclear, biological, and other safety-sensitive topics. The apparent goal was to make an LLM stop analyzing the program or refuse to discuss its contents, rather than to make the strings part of the malware’s actual functionality. This technique is described in the story <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/russia-aligned-uac-0099-plants-nuclear.html">Russia-Aligned UAC-0099 Plants Nuclear Weapon Prompt in Malware to Disrupt AI Analysis</a>. It demonstrates why analysts should not only rely on LLMs for detections and why an LLM’s refusal or interruption is not evidence that the file is safe.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">This does not mean that traditional models are perfect. They can miss new attack patterns, depend on the quality of their features and labels, and require maintenance as the environment changes. In practice, cybersecurity teams often combine methods: a fast traditional model or rules can handle the first pass, while a more capable model can assist with the cases that need additional context and finally a security analyst to review and investigate more complex or higher risk cases.

<h3 id="where-llms-can-make-sense" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Where LLMs Can Make Sense</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">LLMs can be valuable when understanding and combining many kinds of information is more important than processing every event as cheaply and deterministically as possible. For example, they may be useful for:

<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Security alert triage:</span> An LLM can summarize related alerts, logs, and user activity into a timeline and help an analyst decide which investigation to prioritize.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Threat intelligence analysis:</span> An LLM can extract indicators, techniques, and relationships from long incident reports, advisories, and unstructured research, then connect that information to an organization’s existing knowledge base.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Analyst assistance:</span> An LLM can translate a question into a query, explain an unfamiliar command or log entry, and suggest investigation steps. A human or a deterministic system should still validate the result before taking action.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Incident response and reporting:</span> An LLM can help draft a situation report, summarize evidence for different audiences, or compare an incident with previous cases. This can reduce repetitive writing while leaving final conclusions to the response team.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Security engineering and code review:</span> An LLM can reason about unfamiliar code, configuration, and documentation across multiple files, helping identify possible weaknesses or propose tests that a narrowly trained classifier would not recognize.</li>
</ul>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">These use cases benefit from general-purpose reasoning, language understanding, and the ability to work across different document and data formats. They also allow for human review, approval steps, access controls, and logging. A practical design is therefore often a layered system: use rules and traditional ML for fast, high-volume, predictable decisions, and use LLMs selectively where their broader context and generalized intelligence can outweigh their cost, latency, and uncertainty.

<hr style="box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<h2 id="cybersecurity-machine-learning-careers-and-trends" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">Cybersecurity Machine Learning Careers and Trends</h2>

<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Machine learning in cybersecurity is a growing field. The area was considered among top trends by <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/risk-and-resilience/our-insights/cybersecurity/cybersecurity-trends-looking-over-the-horizon">McKinsey</a> in 2022.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">In the <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://www.comptia.org/content/research/cybersecurity-trends-research">CompTIA State of Cybersecurity 2024</a> it says last year there were 660,000 unfilled Cybersecurity positions. <hr style="box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<h2 id="quick-start" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">Quick Start</h2>
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Choose one environment to work in: your host machine (native), the VS Code Dev Container, or the class VM. Each option has a dedicated section below with step-by-step instructions.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">If you already use an IDE (PyCharm or VS Code) and can install conda locally, the Host Setup is the fastest path. Use the Dev Container (lighter weight) or VM (a bit more resource intensive and may not be released by the time our project releases) if you do not want to mess with your local python installation or want an easy way to delete all project setup after the project/class finishes. Finally if you already use proxmox or want to try hosting the VM in proxmox we have a quick section that explains that process based on previous students guides in Ed Discussion.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="which-environment-should-i-use" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">Which environment should I use?</h2>
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Host (native)</span> — Pros: easiest to open files in local IDEs (PyCharm/VS Code) and fastest iteration; Cons: requires installing and managing conda locally.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">VS Code Dev Container</span> — Pros: reproducible environment across machines, no local Python/conda required once container is running; Cons: needs Docker/Podman and VS Code’s Dev Containers extension.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Class VM</span> — Pros: works with setup script and VM is used by other class projects; Cons: may not be released by the start of the ML project, the VM will be slower for GUI IDEs than your native host and is limited by the resources you can allocate to the VM. For M series Mac users the VM will likely be the worst option of the 3.</li>
</ul>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">The project can be done on your host machine, or you can do it on the VM if you don’t want to install conda locally. Regardless of your choice, you will be working with the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing</code> directory that contains all the project files.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">There is a <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">src</code> directory in <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing</code> that contains the project files you will work on. <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Do not move these source files</span> (task1.py through task5.py). The tests in the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">tests</code> dir require the source files to be in <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">src</code>.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Host machine users will start <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="http://github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/setup.html#miniconda-installation-on-your-host-machine">below on the first instructions link</a> by installing Miniconda and the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">cs6035_ML</code> environment. Then you can set up the project in your favorite IDE. We demonstrate set up with PyCharm and VS Code below.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">VM users, please start with the <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="http://github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/setup.html#project-installation-on-the-vm">instructions for installing on the VM</a>.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">There are also <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="http://github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/setup.html#project-setup--getting-started-videos-1">videos if you prefer</a> that to following written instructions.

<h2 id="project-installation-on-your-host-machine" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">Project Installation on your Host Machine</h2>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Host Installation Instructions</span>

<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">You may have heard of <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://www.anaconda.com/">Anaconda, “The Operating System of AI.”</a> It’s a full-featured data science environment that includes everything from a Python environment (conda) to apps including the Spyder IDE.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">For this project we only need the conda part</span>, so we’ll have you download and install <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://docs.anaconda.com/miniconda/">Miniconda from their installer page</a>.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Note: There are graphical installers for the Windows and Mac platforms. In a video below we cover the graphical Windows video installer. If you are on a Mac or running Linux, you can use a bash-based installation script.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">During the conda installation, generally accept the default options provided:</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">In Windows, <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">do not</span> add conda to your path, <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">do</span> register it as the primary Python.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;">On Macs, make sure the installer shows you the “Destination Select” page, otherwise you have to set the installation location earlier in the installation. For Mac issues, <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/install/macos.html">please see the conda Mac docs</a>.

</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Once you have conda installed, you need to install a new conda environment:</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">In Windows, open an “Anaconda Powershell Prompt.”</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">On a Mac or Linux, just open a terminal window normally.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Download the project Student_Local_Testing.zip file from Canvas and unzip it.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">In your terminal window, use the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">cd</code> command to navigate into the Student_Local_Testing directory you unzipped.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Run <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">ls</code> to confirm you have the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">env.yml</code> file in the Student_Local_Testing directory.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Run the following conda command:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">conda env create -f env.yml</code></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;">This will take a couple minutes to complete, if you get timeouts, you can run the following command:

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">conda config --set remote_read_timeout_secs 180.0</code>

</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">(set higher as needed, the 180 is in seconds)</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Once the command finished, confirm the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">cs6035_ML</code> conda env was installed:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">conda activate cs6035_ML</code></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">The prompt will now display <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">(cs6035_ML)</code> where it used to show <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">(base)</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="pycharm-specific-instructions" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">PyCharm-Specific Instructions</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">For Pycharm, you will create a new project and tell Pycharm to use an existing environment, the conda cs6035_ML environment you installed in the above steps.

<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">In Pycharm, choose New Project:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/ML-Python-Project.png?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="Image of Pycharm New Project setup dialog">

<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Be sure the directory name where your project files live is in the Name field (use Student_Local_Testing).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">The location field points to the parent directory of dir in the Name field (wherever you unzipped Student_Local_Testing).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Choose “Custom Environment.”</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Choose “Select Existing.”</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">For Type, if it’s not already chosen, choose “Conda.”</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Be sure the “Path to conda” is filled, if not, point it to the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">conda.bat</code> in the <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">condabin</code> directory in your Miniconda installation.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;">For example, in Windows the Miniconda is capitalized, it won’t be in Linux or Macs: <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">C:\Users\jimlo\Miniconda3\condabin\conda.bat</code></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Once you find your conda executable, then the Environment drop-down should auto-populate with your conda environments.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Select the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">cs6035_ML</code> from the list.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">When you click “Create” you’ll get a dialog confirming you want to create a project where files already exist.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Choose “Create From Existing Files” in this dialog.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="vs-code-specific-instructions" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">VS Code Specific Instructions</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">NOTE: If you’re using VS Code on the VM, you will need to install the Python and Python Debugger extensions. Use View-&gt;Extensions.

<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">VS Code is not a Python-only IDE like PyCharm so we have to have a few things setup there.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">First be sure the official Microsoft <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Python</code> and <code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Python Debugging</code> Extensions are installed.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/VSCode-Extensions.png?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="Python and Python Debugging Extensions Installed"></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Make sure to <em style="box-sizing: border-box;">DENY/REFUSE</em> all the copilot pop-ups to install it or use it. Copilot usage is not allowed in this class even in the IDE as mentioned in the syllabus.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Next you need to select the conda Python interpreter you installed.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Use Ctrl-Shift-P (Windows) to bring up a dialog at the top of the screen.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Enter <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;"><em style="box-sizing: border-box;">select interpreter</em></span> into the text entry area to match the <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;"><em style="box-sizing: border-box;">Python: Select Interpreter</em></span> item.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/Notebook-VSCode-Python-Select-Intpreter-Option.png?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="Select Interpreter option in VS Code"></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Choose the <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;"><em style="box-sizing: border-box;">Python: Select Interpreter</em></span> option.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/Notebook-VSCode-Python-Select-cs6035_ML.png?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="Select Interpreter in VS Code"></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Choose the conda <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">cs6035_ML</span> environment (you may see a different Python version).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Now, to open the project files in VS Code, choose <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">File-&gt;Add Folder to Workspace</span> and select the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing</code> directory.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Make sure that the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing</code> directory is the top level directory in VS Code for tests to work properly.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/ML-on-CLAMP-vs-code-dir.gif?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="Image of VS Code directory structure"></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Now you need to set up tests in VS Code:</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Click on the Beaker Icon, then click on the Configure Tests button:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/ML-docs-beaker-configure-tests.gif?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="Beaker panel with Configure Tests button"></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">Configure tests: Click the beaker icon in the sidebar, then “Configure Tests” &gt; Select <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">unittest</code> &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">tests</code> directory &gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">test_*.py</code> pattern.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">You should see the tests showing in the Tests/Beaker panel:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/ML-docs-showing-tests.gif?w=980&amp;ssl=1" alt="showing tests in panel"></li>
</ul>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">If you get errors debugging tests in VS code, where VS Code reports you are on a pre-3.7 version of Python, read this section:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">If VS Code reports Python version 3.1.x:</span>

<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">There’s a bug currently in the VS Code Python and/or Python Debugger Extensions</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">When you go to Configure the Python Version, you’ll see 3.1.x reported as the version.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">This causes VS Code’s extensions to think you’re running a really old Python version.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">To fix this, go into the View-&gt;Extensions menu and choose the pre-release versions of both the Python and Python Debugger extensions<br style="box-sizing: border-box;"><img data-recalc-dims="1" style="box-sizing: border-box; border-style: none;" src="https://i0.wp.com/github.gatech.edu/pages/cs6035-tools/cs6035-tools.github.io/Projects/Machine_Learning/images/vscode-extension-choose-pre-release-versions.png?w=980&amp;ssl=1"></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="project-installation-in-a-vs-code-dev-container" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">Project Installation in a VS Code Dev Container</h2>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Dev Containers in Visual Studio Code allow you to develop inside a container (via Docker or compatible engines like Podman), providing an isolated, reproducible environment without installing dependencies directly on your host machine. This is useful for ensuring consistency across different systems and avoiding conflicts with local setups. The project will use Miniconda and the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">cs6035_ML</code> environment defined in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">env.yml</code>, running inside the container.

<h3 id="prerequisites" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Prerequisites</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Before setting up the Dev Container, ensure the following are installed and configured on your host machine:

<ol style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style-type: none; counter-reset: step-counter 0; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Install Visual Studio Code</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Download and install VS Code from the official website: <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://code.visualstudio.com/">https://code.visualstudio.com/</a>.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">This is required as the base IDE for Dev Containers.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Install a Container Engine</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Option 1: Docker (Recommended for simplicity)</span>
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1411px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Windows or macOS</span>: Download and install Docker Desktop from <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop">https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop</a>. Follow the installation wizard, and ensure Docker is running (you’ll see the Docker icon in your system tray/menu bar).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Linux</span>: Install Docker Engine following the official docs for your distribution (e.g., <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/">Ubuntu instructions</a>). Start the Docker service with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">sudo systemctl start docker</code> and add your user to the Docker group with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">sudo usermod -aG docker $USER</code> (log out and back in for changes to take effect).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Verify with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">docker --version</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">docker run hello-world</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Option 2: Podman (Daemonless/rootless alternative – see Podman-specific setup below)</span><br style="box-sizing: border-box;">Podman is fully compatible with the Docker CLI in most cases (especially Podman v4+ or v5+), so the Dev Containers extension can use it with minimal changes.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Install the Dev Containers Extension in VS Code</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Open VS Code.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Go to the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X or Cmd+Shift+X on macOS).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Search for “Dev Containers” (published by Microsoft).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Install the extension.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Restart VS Code if prompted.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="podman-specific-setup-alternative-to-docker" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Podman-Specific Setup (Alternative to Docker)</h3>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important;">Podman works as a drop-in replacement for most Docker CLI commands and is officially acknowledged by VS Code as a viable alternative (though not fully officially supported in all edge cases). Use these steps if you prefer Podman (e.g., for rootless operation or avoiding Docker Desktop licensing).

<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Install Podman</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">macOS</span>: Use Homebrew: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">brew install podman</code>, then initialize a machine: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">podman machine init</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">podman machine start</code>.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Windows</span>: Install Podman Desktop or use WSL2 + Podman in a Linux distro.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Linux (Fedora/Ubuntu/etc.)</span>: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">sudo dnf install podman</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">sudo apt install podman</code> (and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">podman-compose</code> if needed for compose support).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Configure VS Code to use Podman</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Open VS Code Settings (Ctrl+, or Cmd+, on macOS).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Search for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">dev.containers.dockerPath</code>.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Set <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Docker: Path</span> to the path of the Podman executable (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">/usr/bin/podman</code> on Linux/macOS, or the full path to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">podman.exe</code> on Windows).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">(Optional but recommended for rootless Podman) Search for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">dev.containers.dockerComposePath</code> and set it to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">/usr/bin/podman-compose</code> (or equivalent) if using compose features.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">For rootless Podman compatibility issues (e.g., UID mapping), add the following to your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">devcontainer.json</code> under top-level properties:
<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; background-color: #f5f6fa; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: none; position: relative; padding: 0px;">
<div class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial; overflow-x: auto; padding: 0.75rem; border: 0px;">
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"runArgs"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">[</span><span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"--userns=keep-id"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">]</span><span class="err" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ffffff; background-color: #e05151;">,</span>
<span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"containerUser"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"vscode"</span><span class="err" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ffffff; background-color: #e05151;">,</span>
<span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"updateRemoteUserUID"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="kc" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #a625a4;">true</span><span class="err" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ffffff; background-color: #e05151;">,</span>
<span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"containerEnv"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{</span> <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"HOME"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"/home/vscode"</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">}</span>
</code></pre>
</div>
&nbsp;

</div>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Enable the Podman socket if needed (Linux): <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">systemctl --user enable --now podman.socket</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Troubleshooting Podman</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">If builds fail due to socket issues, ensure the Podman socket is active (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">podman system service --time=0 &amp;</code> in a background terminal).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Some advanced Docker features (e.g., buildx) may require extra flags or have limitations; test simple containers first.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Install the “Podman” extension in VS Code for better Podman integration (optional but helpful).</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="setting-up-the-project-in-a-dev-container" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Setting up the Project in a Dev Container</h3>
<ol style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style-type: none; counter-reset: step-counter 0; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Prepare the Project Files</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Download the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing.zip</code> file from Canvas and unzip it to a local directory (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">~/projects/Student_Local_Testing</code>).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Open this directory in VS Code: Go to File &gt; Open Folder and select the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing</code> folder.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Create the Dev Container Configuration</span>:
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">In the project root (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Student_Local_Testing</code>), create a new folder named <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">.devcontainer</code> (include the dot).</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;">Inside <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">.devcontainer</code>, create a file named <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">devcontainer.json</code> with the following content:

<div class="language-json highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; background-color: #f5f6fa; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: none; position: relative; padding: 0px;">
<div class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial; overflow-x: auto; padding: 0.75rem; border: 0px;">
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"name"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"CS6035 Machine Learning Project"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">,</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"image"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"continuumio/miniconda3"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">,</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"features"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{},</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"postCreateCommand"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"conda config --set remote_read_timeout_secs 180.0 &amp;&amp; conda env create -f env.yml"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">,</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"postAttachCommand"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"conda init bash"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">,</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"customizations"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{</span>
   <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"vscode"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{</span>
     <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"extensions"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">[</span>
       <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"ms-python.python"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">,</span>
       <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"ms-python.debugpy"</span>
     <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">],</span>
     <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"settings"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{</span>
       <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"python.defaultInterpreterPath"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"/opt/conda/envs/cs6035_ML/bin/python"</span>
     <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">}</span>
   <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">}</span>
 <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">},</span>
 <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"remoteEnv"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">{</span>
   <span class="nl" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #ca7601;">"PATH"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span> <span class="s2" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"${containerEnv:PATH}:/opt/conda/bin:/opt/conda/condabin"</span>
 <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">}</span>
 <span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">}</span>
</code></pre>
</div>
&nbsp;

</div>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
