<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Example of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">feature_engineering_functions</code>:

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<div class="language-python highlighter-rouge" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; background-color: #f5f6fa; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: none; position: relative; padding: 0px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;">
<div class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial; overflow-x: auto; padding: 0.75rem; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;">
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"><span class="k" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #a625a4;">def</span> <span class="nf" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">double_height</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">(</span><span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">dataframe</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span><span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">pd</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">.</span><span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">DataFrame</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">):</span>
    <span class="k" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #a625a4;">return</span> <span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">dataframe</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">[</span><span class="s" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #50a04f;">"height"</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">]</span> <span class="o" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">*</span> <span class="mi" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #b66a00;">2</span>

<span class="k" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #a625a4;">def</span> <span class="nf" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">half_height</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">(</span><span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">dataframe</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">:</span><span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">pd</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">.</span><span class="n" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">DataFrame</span><span class="p" style="box-sizing: border-box; color: #383942;">):</span>

<h2 id="preprocessdatasetone_hot_encode_columns_train-and-one_hot_encode_columns_test" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">PreprocessDataset:<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">one_hot_encode_columns_train</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">one_hot_encode_columns_test</code></h2>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">One Hot Encoding is the process of taking a column and returning a binary vector representing the various values within it. There is a separate function for the training and test datasets since they should be handled separately to avoid data leakage (see the 3rd link in Useful Resources for a little more info on how to handle them).

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<h3 id="pseudocode" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">Pseudocode</h3>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">one_hot_encode_columns_train()</code>

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<ol style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style-type: none; counter-reset: step-counter 0; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">In the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">PreprocessDataset</code> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">__init__()</code> method initialize an instance variable containing a scikit-learn <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">OneHotEncoder</code> with any parameters you may need.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Split <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">train_features</code> into two DataFrames: one with only the columns you want to one hot encode (using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">one_hot_encode_cols</code>) and another with all the other columns.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Fit the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">OneHotEncoder</code> using the DataFrame you split from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">train_features</code> with the columns you want to encode.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Transform the DataFrame you split from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">train_features</code> with the columns you want to encode using the fitted <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">OneHotEncoder</code>.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Create a DataFrame from the 2D array of data that the output from step 4 gave you, with column names in the form of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">columnName_categoryName</code> (there should be an attribute in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">OneHotEncoder</code> that can help you with this) and the same index that <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">train_features</code> had.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Concatenate the DataFrame you made in step 5 with the DataFrame of other columns from step 2.</li>
</ol>

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Note:</span> For the local tests and autograder use the column naming scheme of joining the previous column name and the column value with an underscore (similar to above where Type -&gt; Type_Fruit and Type_Vegetable)

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Note 2:</span> Since you should only be fitting your encoder on the training data, if there are values in your test set that are different than those in the training set, you will denote that with 0s. In the example above, let’s say we have a row in the test set with pizza, which is neither a fruit nor vegetable for the Type_Fruit and Type_Vegetable. It should result in a 0 for both columns. If you don’t handle these properly, you may get errors like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">Test Failed: Found unknown categories</code>.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Note 3:</span> You may be tempted to use the pandas function <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">get_dummies</code> to solve this task, but its a trap. It seems easier, but you will have to do a lot more work to make it handle a train/test split. So, we suggest you use scikit-learn’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">OneHotEncoder</code>.

<h2 id="preprocessdatasetmin_max_scaled_columns_train-and-min_max_scaled_columns_test" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">PreprocessDataset:<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">min_max_scaled_columns_train</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">min_max_scaled_columns_test</code></h2>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Min/Max Scaling is a process to transform numerical features to a specific range, typically [0, 1], to ensure that input values are comparable (similar to how you may have heard of “normalizing” data) and is a crucial preprocessing step for many machine learning algos. In particular this standardization is essential for algorithms like linear regression, logistic regression, k-means, and neural networks, which can be sensitive to the scale of input features, whereas some algos like decision trees are less impacted.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">By applying Min/Max Scaling, we prevent feature dominance, to ideally improve performance and accuracy of these algorithms and improve training convergence. It’s a recommended step to ensure your models are trained on consistent and standardized data.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">For the provided assignment you should <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">use the scikit-learn MinMaxScaler function</span> (linked in the resources below) rather than attempting to implement your own scaling function.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">The <em style="box-sizing: border-box;">rough</em> implementation of the scikit-learn function is provided below for educational purposes.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Note: There are separate functions for the training and test datasets to help avoid data leakage between the test/train datasets. Please refer to the 3rd link in Useful Resources for more information on how to handle this – namely that we should still scale the test data based on our “knowledge” of the train dataset.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

<h2 id="preprocessdatasetpca_train-and-pca_test" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">PreprocessDataset:<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">pca_train</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">pca_test</code></h2>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Principal Component Analysis is a dimensionality reduction technique (column reduction). It aims to take the variance in your input columns and map the columns into N columns that contain as much of the variance as it can. This technique can be useful if you are trying to train a model faster and has some more advanced uses, especially when training models on data which has many columns but few rows. There is a separate function for the training and test datasets because they should be handled separately to avoid data leakage (see the 3rd link in Useful Resources for a little more info on how to handle them).

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Note 1:</span> For the local tests and autograder, use the following column naming scheme: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">component_1</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">component_2</code>, …, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">component_n</code>, where <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">n</code> is the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">n_components</code> value passed to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">__init__</code> method.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Note 2:</span> For your PCA outputs to match the local tests and autograder, make sure you set the seed using a random state of 0 when you initialize the PCA function.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Note 3:</span> Since PCA does not work with NA values, make sure you drop any columns that have NA values before running PCA.

<h2 id="preprocessdatasetfeature_engineering_train-feature_engineering_test" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;">PreprocessDataset:<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">feature_engineering_train</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">feature_engineering_test</code></h2>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Feature Engineering is a process of using domain knowledge (physics, geometry, sports statistics, business metrics, etc.) to create new features (columns) out of the existing data. This could mean creating an area feature when given the length and width of a triangle or extracting the major and minor version number from a software version or more complex logic depending on the scenario.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">In cybersecurity in particular, feature engineering is crucial for using domain expert’s (e.g. a security analyst) experience to identify anomalous behavior that might signify a security breach. This could involve creating features that represent deviations from established baselines, such as unusual file access patterns, unexpected network connections, or sudden spikes in CPU usage. These anomaly-based features can help distinguish malicious activity from normal system operations, but the system does not know what data patterns mean anomalous off-hand – that is where you as the domain expert can help by creating features.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">These methods utilize a dictionary, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">feature_engineering_functions</code>, <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">passed to the class constructor (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; font-weight: 400; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">__init__</code>)</span>. This dictionary defines how to generate new features:

<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Keys:</span> Strings representing new column names.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Values:</span> Functions that:

<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Now, we will put three of the above methods together into a preprocess function. This function will take in a dataset and perform <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">encoding</span>, <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">scaling</span>, and <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">feature engineering</span> using the above methods and their respective columns. You should <span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">not</span> perform PCA for this function.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

<h2 id="task-3-15--points" style="letter-spacing: normal; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.5rem 0px 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 36px !important;" class="akch-demoted-h1">Task 3 (15 points)</h2>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<hr style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;">
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">In Task 2 you learned how to split a dataset into training and testing components. Now it’s time to learn about using a K-means model. We will run a basic model on the data to cluster files (rows) with similar attributes together. We will use an unsupervised model.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<hr style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;">
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">Theory</span>

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">An <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsupervised_learning">unsupervised model</a> has no label column. By contrast, in <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supervised_learning">supervised learning</a> (which you’ll see in Task 4) the data has features and targets/labels. These labels are effectively an answer key to the data in the feature columns. You don’t have this answer key in unsupervised learning, instead you’re working on data without labels. You’ll need to use algorithms that learn directly from the data without the benefit of labels.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">We start with <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-means_clustering">K-means</a> because it is simple to understand the algorithm. For the mathematical people, you can look at the underlying data structure, <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voronoi_diagram">a Voronoi diagram</a>. Based on squared <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance">Euclidean distances</a>, K-means creates clusters of similar datapoints. Each cluster has a centroid. The idea is that for each sample, it’s associated/clustered with the centroid that is the “closest.”

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Closest is an interesting concept in higher dimensions. You can think of each feature in a dataset as a dimension in the data. If it’s 2D or 3D, we can visualize it easily. Concepts of distance are easy to visualize in 2D and 3D, and they extend similarly to higher dimensions.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">If you read the Wikipedia articles for K-means you’ll see a discussion of the use of “squared Euclidean distances” in K-means. This is compared with simple Euclidean distances in the Weber problem, and better approaches resulting from k-medians and k-mediods is discussed.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<hr style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: content-box; overflow: visible; margin: 2rem 0px; padding: 0px; background-color: #eeebee; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;">
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Please use scikit-learn to create the model and Yellowbrick to determine the optimal value of k for the dataset.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

Now, we will run a basic model on the data to cluster files (rows) with similar attributes together. We will use an unsupervised model (model with no label column), K-means. Again, use scikit-learn to create the model and Yellowbrick to determine the optimal value of k for the dataset.

<h2 id="local-test-dataset-information" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-size: 24px !important;">Local Test Dataset Information</h2>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em;">For this task the local test dataset we are using is the NATICUSdroid dataset, which contains 86 columns of data related to android permissions used by benign and malicious Android applications released between 2010 and 2019. For more information such as the introductory paper and the Citations/Acknowledgements you can view the <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/722/naticusdroid+android+permissions+dataset">dataset</a> site in the UCI ML repository. In this specific case clustering can be a useful tool to group apps that request similar permissions together. The team that created this dataset hypothesized that malicious apps would exhibit distinct patterns in the types of permissions they request compared to benign apps. This difference in permission request patterns could potentially be used to distinguish between malicious and benign applications.

<h3 id="kmeansclusteringkmeans_get_n_clusters" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 18px !important;">KmeansClustering:<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">kmeans_get_n_clusters</code></h3>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">K-means clustering is a process of grouping similar rows together and assigning them to a cluster. For this method, you will use the training data to fit an optimal K-means cluster on the data.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Initialize a scikit-learn K-means model with the parameters passed to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">__init__</code> method

</ul>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; position: relative; color: #000000 !important;">Try to find the best <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">k</code> to use for K-means clustering.
<ul style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1435px;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Initialize a Yellowbrick KElbowVisualizer with the K-means model.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px;">Use that visualizer to search for the optimal value of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">k</code> (between 2 inclusive and 10 exclusive; in mathematical notation, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">[2,10)</code>).</li>
</ul>

For this method you will use the trained model from the previous task to fit an optimal K-means cluster on the test data.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>

<h2 id="local-test-dataset-information" style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-size: 24px !important;">Local Test Dataset Information</h2>
<p style="box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em;">For this task the local test dataset we are using is the NATICUSdroid dataset, which contains 86 columns of data related to android permissions used by benign and malicious Android applications released between 2010 and 2019. For more information such as the introductory paper and the Citations/Acknowledgements you can view the <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/722/naticusdroid+android+permissions+dataset">dataset</a> site in the UCI ML repository. If you look at the <a style="box-sizing: border-box; background-color: transparent; color: #7253ed; text-decoration: underline #eeebee; text-underline-offset: 2px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;" href="https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/NDSS2021posters_paper_12.pdf">online poster</a> for the paper that the dataset creators wrote from their research, they trained a variety of different models including Random Forest, Logistic Regression and XGBoost and calculated a variety of metrics related to training and detection performance. In this task we will guide you through training ML models and calculating performance metrics to compare the predictive abilities of different models.

</li>
</ul>

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<ul style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 0.5em; padding-left: 1.5em; list-style: none; width: 1459px; color: #5c5962; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">In order to simplify the autograding we have created a class that will hold the metrics and feature importances for a model you trained.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">You should not modify this class but are expected to use it in your return statements.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">This means you put your training and test metrics dictionaries and feature importance DataFrames inside a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">ModelMetrics</code> object for the autograder to handle. This is for each of the Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest models you will create.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0.25em 0px; color: #000000 !important;">You do not need to return a feature importance DataFrame in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">ModelMetrics</code> value for the naive model you will create, just return None in that position of the return statement, as the given code does.</li>
</ul>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<h2 id="calculate_naive_metrics" style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0.25em; line-height: 1.25; position: relative; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important; font-size: 24px !important;"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">calculate_naive_metrics</code></h2>
<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">A Naive model is a very simple model/prediction that can help to frame how well a more sophisticated model is doing. At best, such a model has random competence at predicting things. At worst, it’s wrong all the time.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;">Since a naive model is incredibly basic (often a constant or randomly selected result), we can expect that any more sophisticated model that we train should outperform it. If the naive Model beats our trained model, it can mean that additional data (rows or columns) is needed in the dataset to improve our model. It can also mean that the dataset doesn’t have a strong enough signal for the target we want to predict.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
<p style="white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, blinkmacsystemfont, 'Segoe UI', roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000 !important;"><span style="box-sizing: border-box; font-weight: bolder;">In this function, you’ll implement a simple model that always predicts a constant (function-provided) number, regardless of the input values.</span> Specifically, you’ll use a given constant integer, provided as the parameter <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.2em 0.15em; background-color: #f5f6fa; border: 1px solid #eeebee; border-radius: 4px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; color: #000000 !important;">naive_assumption</code>, as the model’s prediction. This means the model will always output this constant value, without considering the actual data. Afterward, you will calculate four metrics—accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score—for both the training and test datasets.

<pre class="highlight" style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: monospace, monospace; font-size: 1em; margin: 0px; background: #f5f6fa; overflow-wrap: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; padding: 0px; border: 0px;"><code style="box-sizing: border-box; font-family: SFMono-Regular, menlo, consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75em; line-height: 1.4; overflow-x: auto; overflow-wrap: break-word; padding: 0px; border: 0px; color: #000000 !important;"></code></pre>
